questions.q: In what year does David begin the story of his adventures?
Who was waiting for David by the garden gate of the manse?
choices: The new dominie who would run the school
Mr. Campbell, the minister of Essendean
His uncle Ebenezer Balfour of Shaws
Mrs. Campbell with a basket of food
questions.evidence: Mr. Campbell, the minister of Essendean, was waiting for me

choices: His father has sent him to find work
He wants to join the army in Edinburgh
He has been sent away from the school
Both of his parents have died

questions.q: What did David's father leave for him, which he called David's inheritance?
choices: A map showing the way to Cramond
A letter to be taken to the house of Shaws
The deed to the schoolhouse at Essendean
A small purse of gold coins and a ring
questions.evidence: he gave me in charge a certain letter, which he said was your inheritance

questions.q: To whom was the letter addressed?
choices: The minister of the kirk at Cramond parish
Ebenezer Balfour, Esquire, of Shaws
Mr. Campbell of Kilrennet
Alexander Balfour of Edinburgh
questions.evidence: To the hands of Ebenezer Balfour, Esquire, of Shaws

questions.q: How old is David when he sets off on his journey?
choices: Fourteen
Seventeen
Twelve
Twenty-one
questions.evidence: a lad of seventeen years of age

questions.q: What did Mr. Campbell say David could do if his relations at Shaws turned him away?
choices: Look for work as a teacher in Edinburgh
Walk the two days back and come to the manse
Write a letter to the minister asking for money
Take a ship from Cramond to find his fortune
questions.evidence: ye can but walk the two days back again and risp at the manse door

questions.q: Mr. Campbell tells David, "Be soople, Davie, in things immaterial." What does "soople" mean here?
choices: Proud and ready to stand up for yourself
Quick to run away from any danger
Willing to bend and go along with others
Careful to keep your money hidden
questions.evidence: Be soople, Davie, in things immaterial

questions.q: What was the "round" gift in Mr. Campbell's little packet?
choices: A ball of sealing wax
A wooden button
A shilling piece
A small silver watch
questions.evidence: That which he had called round, I found to be a shilling piece

questions.q: What was the "cubical" gift that Mr. Campbell hoped would see David "into a better land"?
choices: A small block of cheese
A little Bible
A box of medicine
A carved wooden box
questions.evidence: sure enough it was a little Bible

questions.q: What was written on the flat, square piece of yellow paper?
choices: A list of David's relations at Shaws
Directions for the road from Essendean to Cramond
A prayer to keep travellers safe on a journey
A recipe for lily of the valley water
questions.evidence: TO MAKE LILLY OF THE VALLEY WATER

questions.q: Why did David's conscience smite him after Mr. Campbell ran off?
choices: He had forgotten to thank Mrs. Campbell for her gifts
He had sold his father's books for far too little money
The minister was sad, but David was glad to leave
He had lied to the minister about breakfast
questions.evidence: I, for my part, was overjoyed to get away

questions.q: What was the last thing David looked back at as he left?
choices: The big boulder under the birch by the trackside
Kirk Essendean, the manse and the kirkyard
The ford where Mr. Campbell had turned back home
His father's house on Essen-Waterside
questions.evidence: I took my last look of Kirk Essendean

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: David and the minister quarrelling over money
David arriving at a great, busy house near Edinburgh
David leaving his home village for the house of Shaws
David learning that his father was secretly a rich laird
questions.evidence: start him off to the house of Shaws
